pool.text: The Grand Bazaar began operating as one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets.
The first Turkish newspaper, Takvim-i Vekayi, was published in the former Ottoman capital.
Horse-drawn trams were introduced in Istanbul, marking the early history of the city's trams.
The Tünel opened as the world's second-oldest subterranean rail line after London.
International rail service launched with a line between Bucharest and Sirkeci Terminal.
The Silahtarağa Power Station completed its first engine room as a sole electricity source.
The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality was established as the main citywide local government authority.
The airport became a civilian airport and the hub of Turkish Airlines.
The first international flight took place between Istanbul and Athens.
The airport terminal building was opened and later featured in a James Bond film.
The Istanbul Biennial began holding contemporary art exhibitions biennially.
The annual Istanbul Jazz Festival was established to be held every year.
The American news channel CNN licensed its brand to the Turkish-language CNN Türk.
Sabiha Gökçen International Airport opened as the main airport on the Asian side.
Emirgan Park began holding an annual tulip festival known for its plant diversity.
A more modern funicular between Taksim Square and Kabataş began running.
The contactless Istanbulkart was introduced to integrate fares across transportation modes.
The Istanbul Shopping Fest began as an annual shopping festival held in the city.
The Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge entered service on August 26.
A marine mucilage wave allegedly caused by water pollution spread to Sea of Marmara.
